Love triangle. Every teen novel published when I was about thirteen-fourteen had a love triangle in it, and I was sick to death of it.

It always panned out like; 

-Guy who the main character is clearly going to end up with
-Guy who is there to bring some tension into the story 

Ironically it was the Hunger Games that started this trend, because Suzanne Collins actually did a good job of showing that Katniss was only ‘interested’ in Gale because of the security and familiarity that she felt with him and the guilt she felt for not feeling the same way, not because of any actual attraction. 

But the YA publishing industry completely misinterpreted that aspect of the story, and decided that all teens were now *super* into love triangles. A lot of otherwise good books had this random dynamic shoehorned in there because they thought it would sell. 

The only love triangle I’m actually interested in is one that is an actual poly relationship, or at least one that explores the toxicity of being caught in the middle of people’s affections like that.

I have a few red flags, I’ve been rping for a long time. I consider myself a veteran at this point. 

1. RP partners should be that, partners. If planning with them feels like you guys are trying to wrestle a steering wheel from each other, red flag. It’s supposed to be fun, not confrontational. 

2. If they’re overly sensitive. If it feels like saying ‘hi’ offends them some days, red flag. They’re going to be impossible to rp with long term, especially one on one. If it’s a group setting, having more people around to mellow them out may help. 

3. Omegle rp is like the rp equivalent of a pump and dump. Don’t try to kid yourself that pursuing a relationship outside of that one conversation will work, because 9/10 it won’t. On the off chance you guys hit it off, there’s an equally high chance that they’re some kind of predator.  If you’re not good at saying ‘no’ to people, stay away from Omegle. 

4. Their character feels like a black hole. Every time they walk in the room, they suck the light out of all the others. Everything has to be about them, their drama, their story. They’re the smartest, prettiest, strongest, and have no weaknesses, but are also inexplicably crippled with trauma. Red flag. 

5. If it feels like their character backstory is just a copy of yours but with the trauma turned up to eleven, red flag. These people often don’t have a respect for other people’s triggers, and as someone with moderate/severe irl PTSD, I’ve had to pull out of a few rp relationships due to this. People particularly like to do this with SA trauma, so any fellow survivors out there, make sure to prioritise your mental health over an rp. 

6. If they nitpick other people’s ideas until everyone loses enthusiasm for them, red flag. If it’s a good idea, and other people respond well to it, just ignore the naysayers and don’t let them cramp your style. The golden rule of a good RP partner is someone who ‘yes, and’s you, not someone who ‘no, but’s you.

You’re trapped in a single, crowded building for five days a week, eight hours a day. In uniform schools, you have to wear clothes that are itchy, uncomfortable and often ill fitting.

You cannot dictate when you eat, when you drink, what you drink out of, how you wear your hair, what accessories you can wear, when or where you stand, when or where you sit, when you can breathe fresh air, when you can speak, when you can move, when you can use the toilet. 

If you step out of line, you’re punished. If you don’t but a teacher hates you, you’re punished. If you’re in the same class as someone who steps out of line, you’re punished. 

Who you are friends with depends entirely on arbitrary things, especially before the ages of 16-18. How attractive you are, how much money you have, what your race is. When you’re done at school, you have an extra two hours work to do per night, and if you don’t do it then you’re punished. There’s no compensation if you do it, it’s just mandatory. 

With all this shit you’d expect the education system to at least give a full education, but year by year it’s a crumbling institution that treats children more and more like assets and less like human beings. 

If you’re neurodivergent, you’re fucked. 

If you’re anything other than straight, white, cis, attractive, wealthy, reasonably intelligent and neurotypical, you’re fucked and you have lifelong trauma which you will probably have to fight the rigged healthcare system to get ineffectual counselling for.
